Q: js and css not loading when hosting next application on GitHub pages A:

I have tried many advices, .nojekyll, different github templates, different folders, branches. It never worked, or the steps were so complicated and confusing - especially for repeated deployments, that it wasn't worth it.

This guide, once set, will work automatically with a push.

How to deploy to github pages

  1. Go to Repo Settings and set Pages > Build and deployment to GitHub Actions.
    Nothing else necessary as the script will be made in the repo in next step.

    • note: only public and org repos are eligible for GitHub Pages
    • e.g. https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/settings/pages

  2. Configure the /.github/workflows/deploy.yml GitHub Action in your repo. Find the file attached below.

  3. Configure /next.config.ts - Find the content attached below.

  4. Add new script to your package.json.

    "scripts": {
  "build:gh-pages": "cross-env PAGES_BASE_PATH=/<eg-your-repo-name> pnpm build",
}
    • <eg-your-repo-name> is the sub-path where your app will be deployed, it can be anything. I chose repo name for consistency.
    • this value is necessary for assets and links to work correctly when not served from root
    • for example, this is my repo name and the resulting deployment url
      • https://github.com/ackvf/ts-mock-generator
      • https://ackvf.github.is/ts-mock-generator

  5. Build the repo locally with

    pnpm run build:gh-pages

  6. Push the /out/ or /dist/ folder to github to main or gh-pages branch.

  7. This will trigger automatic deployment.

/next.config.ts

const nextConfig = {
  /**
   * Static Export
   *
   * Sets the build to static export so that we can
   * host from any static html hosting service.
   *
   * Limitations: https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/static-exports
   */

  output: "export",
  distDir: "out", // this is the default
  basePath: process.env.PAGES_BASE_PATH,
  images: {
    // Allows next/image to be used without 3rd party optimization service. - necessary for static export
    unoptimized: true,
  },
}

/.github/workflows/deploy.yml

This flow takes about 20s as it doesn't build anything, it only copies and pushes the existing artifacts. You can use it to push and host any html, not just next.js.

name: Deploy Next.js site to Pages

# This flow requires the built output in /out/ folder. (configure below)
# note: You need to configure correct PAGES_BASE_PATH and basePath during build.

on:
  # Runs on pushes targeting these branches
  push:
    branches:
      - main      # <- remove main for better control of deployments only via specific branch
      - gh-pages

  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

# Sets permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN to allow deployment to GitHub Pages
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Allow only one concurrent deployment, skipping runs queued between the run in-progress and latest queued.
# However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.
concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  upload:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Pages
        id: setup_pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./out

  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: upload
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

Q: How can I measure CSS parsing and rendering time in a browser? A:

To measure CSS parsing and rendering time:

  • Open DevTools (F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I/Cmd+Option+I).
  • Go to the Performance tab.
  • Record the performance by clicking the record button, then refresh or interact with the page.
  • Stop recording and analyze the results for Style Recalculation and Layout times to see how CSS affects performance.

Q: How to save a Power Query table as a regular table (without connections) in a new workbook? A:

Two steps instead of one, but really easy.

  1. Copy the table (as you were already doing)

  2. Click in the copied table, and choose Table Design > Unlink

    The unlink button localed in the ribbon group "External Table Data" on the Data menu ribbon.

Q: How do I have to configure Visual Studio Code, so I don't get a "undefined reference" error message? A:

I have the same problem and it seems to be a linker error.

You should use the terminal embedded in Visual Studio Code and build your file using the string:

g++ -g -o main main.cpp personne.cpp

Then simply execute the executable file called main. You should also try to add the file personne.cpp to the tasks.json file.

Q: Azure AD login returning unauthorize (401) inspite of having up-to-date configs A:

it seems the issue is likely that your WebClient cannot download the keys from Azure because it is using an old security protocol. Azure requires TLS 1.2, but .NET 4.8 often defaults to an older version.

When the download fails, your app cannot verify the token, which causes the 401 error.

To fix this, add this line in your Global.asax.cs file inside the Application_Start method:

System.Net.ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol = System.Net.SecurityProtocolType.Tls12;

Also, take a look at your foreach loop. You are ignoring keys that do not have x5c data. Sometimes Azure sends keys using just RSA numbers (n and e) without the certificate string. If that happens, your list of tokens might be empty, which would also make the login fail.
